value.answer: For a short time, most adults handle it fine. The NIH says short-term use looks safe for most people, though there isn't much data on long-term use. The long-term question is the open one: a preliminary AHA abstract from November 2025 linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to more heart failure diagnoses. It isn't peer-reviewed, it can't prove cause, and some experts think poor sleep may be behind the difference. If you're thinking of taking it regularly, or you take other meds, check with a doctor or pharmacist first.
